summary: MetalFX offers GPU temporal and spatial upscalers plus frame interpolation, all fed by Metal textures and command buffers. BifrOSt has no upscaling scaler: its nearest code is CPU bilinear resampling and a GL_LINEAR blur pyramid on the GLES presenter, neither of which takes motion, depth or colour-space input.

features.note: Jittered accumulation with depth rejection and neighbourhood clamping is a pure CPU model with host tests, and it is not wired into apps or the shell. Gap: the presenter (springboard/src/gpu/wl.rs:147) receives no motion or depth buffers and the scaler has no GPU pass, so it needs the lab machine to verify.

Denoised accumulation runs a 3x3 box filter on the input colour and keeps 95 percent history, all in the CPU model with host tests. Gap: the box filter is not a learned denoiser, and the GPU path has no temporal history buffer, so the lab machine must verify it.

A CPU Catmull-Rom bicubic upscaler with clamped edges is tested headless in springboard/render/tests/parity_sdk-complete-39.rs (flat rasters stay flat, bad sizes and sample counts are refused). Gap: there is no edge-aware scaler, no temporal input and no GPU path, so it is a resampler rather than a spatial upscaler, and it is not wired into apps or the shell.

Linear, perceptual sRGB and HDR modes are tested headless in springboard/render/tests/parity_sdk-complete-39.rs, including overshoot clamped in linear and kept in HDR. Gap: the mode is passed per call rather than read from a colour-space tag on the raster, and nothing is wired into apps or the shell.

Wave 4 (w4-metalfx, parity/integration 0925691e): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. No frame generation anywhere in the shell or the GPU presenter.

features.feature: Metal command-buffer encoding of scaler passes
features.apple: encode(commandBuffer:) on each effect; MTL4FX* protocols
features.bifrost: springboard/sdk/src/gpu_pass.rs (RenderPass, the checked pass model apps describe their passes with); springboard/src/gpu/wl.rs:147 (Presenter, GLES passes), docs/gpu-first.md
features.note: Metal command buffers and the MTL4FX encode protocols exist only on Apple's GPU drivers, so encoding a scaler into a Metal command buffer cannot exist on an Arch Linux system. The GPU passes that remain are the presenter's GLES render passes (one per present), which stay inside the shell, and apps describe their own passes with the checked RenderPass model.

features.feature: Reduced-resolution GPU work with linear upscale
features.apple: Render at low resolution, upscale to output (MetalFX landing page)
features.bifrost: springboard/sdk/src/gpu_pass.rs (blur_plan, BlurPlan); springboard/src/gpu/wl.rs:724 (blur pyramid upscale, GL_LINEAR), docs/gpu-first.md:85 (quarter-size base), springboard/render/src/gfx.rs:423 (blur_material)
features.note: The divisor, working size and full-size fallback for a reduced copy are tested headless in tests/parity_sdk-os-02.rs. Gap: the linear upscale runs only inside the shell's presenter, and apps get no scaler.

gaps: Motion vectors and depth input for temporal scaling: the presenter has no per-pixel motion or depth buffers.
Spatial upscaler on the GPU: only CPU bilinear resampling exists, in springboard/render/src/gfx.rs and springboard/render/src/gfx/rotate.rs.
Frame interpolation (macOS 26 API) and the temporal denoiser: no counterpart.
App-facing scaler API in bifrost_app: none, so apps cannot request GPU upscaling of their own render targets.
Colour-space-aware scaling (linear, perceptual, HDR modes): the bilinear helpers take no colour-space parameter.
